`entry_kb=$(bounded "$JOURNAL_SCAN_TIMEOUT" du -sk "$entry" ...)` at :637 — du has no cursor bound, so on a timeout-less host it can walk indefinitely

The comment argues the cursor removes the unbounded journal read, but the debris `du` walk (:637) and `git ls-remote` (:1199) have NO cursor equivalent — on a `timeout`-less host those two remain genuinely unbounded, which is the exact §2d failure mode the change is fixing elsewhere.

observability.sh:305 `DOCKER_DU_TIMEOUT="${DOCKER_DU_TIMEOUT:-120}"`

advisory.finding: The observability unit's start-timeout budget claim ("12 scans x 10 s = 120 s < 240 s TimeoutStartSec") counts only journal scans and omits the other bounded commands in the same run: DOCKER_DU_TIMEOUT=120s, DOCKER_DF_TIMEOUT=20s, three IMDS curls at --max-time 5, and git ls-remote at 15s. Their worst-case sum can exceed the 240 s TimeoutStartSec, causing systemd to SIGKILL a healthy-but-slow run mid-write and silently drop that interval's metrics.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider setting an explicit TimeoutStopSec (and confirm KillMode) on both units so the SIGKILL-based bound is enforced even when a child is stuck in uninterruptible I/O.
evidence: install-observability.sh:41 `TimeoutStartSec=240` with no TimeoutStopSec/KillMode set in the [Service] block (lines 27-46)
rebar-autodeploy.service:40 `TimeoutStartSec=90` with no TimeoutStopSec/KillMode
ABSENCE: no `TimeoutStopSec=` or `KillMode=` in either rendered [Service] section
advisory.finding: Both units now depend on systemd SIGKILL (TimeoutStartSec) to bound a hung run, but neither sets TimeoutStopSec or KillMode. Under the exact incident condition (IOPS-saturated volume), a `du`/journalctl child stuck in uninterruptible-sleep (D state) will not respond to SIGKILL promptly, so the run may persist past the intended 240s/90s bound and continue delaying the timer's re-arm.
